Checking whether NotFoundError maps to not_found.

NotFoundError is not mapped in toAppError. It falls through to internal_error. Callers must map it to not_found themselves. TenantScopeError handles cross-workspace access. NotFoundError covers missing or invalid references.

Labels must belong to the workspace. Stale or foreign label IDs should be refused when setting labels. Issues should not display labels from other workspaces.

The lookup strategy for distinguishing missing labels from cross-workspace references is still open. A global or unfiltered query would reveal whether a label exists outside the workspace.

A global label lookup is required to distinguish a foreign label from a missing one. If the label exists in another organization, throw TenantScopeError; otherwise throw NotFoundError. The label repository must support org-free lookups.

Parent issues must be live issues within the same project. A different workspace triggers tenant scope. A different project, archived state, or missing parent triggers not found.

Replies must target a live top-level comment on the same issue. A reply to a comment on a different issue is refused. A comment from another workspace triggers tenant scope. A deleted or missing parent comment, or a reply-to-reply, returns not found.

Assignees must be current members of the workspace. A non-member is refused as not found.

A person is not a workspace-scoped resource. A non-current member is refused as not found. This applies even if the user exists elsewhere or was previously a member.

Mentions of non-current members are dropped rather than refused. Client-provided user IDs that are not current workspace members should be ignored, and @handles for former members are already filtered out by resolveMentions.

content.thinking:
NotFoundError is not mapped in toAppError.

I will throw NotFoundError and TenantScopeError. Cross-workspace lookups by ID must check the actor's org against the row's org to catch tenant scope violations. The codebase requires every repository query to be filtered by org_id.

Repositories always filter by org_id, so foreign rows return null and look like missing records. This makes it impossible to distinguish a genuine not-found from a cross-workspace tenant scope violation.

An unscoped repository lookup by ID would let the service assert org scope separately. The user explicitly requires cross-workspace access to return TenantScopeError.

Not found applies to missing, archived, deleted, inactive members, and parent or reply references. A parent in another workspace triggers TenantScopeError. A parent in another project of the same workspace returns NotFound. Archived parents return NotFound rather than AlreadyArchivedError. An assignee who is not a member of the current organization returns NotFound; membership is checked per organization without looking up other memberships.

Project leads face the same cross-org scope rules. Labels and comments both return TenantScopeError for foreign IDs and NotFound for missing or archived parents. Replies to replies are also rejected as NotFound.

Validation must run before any repository write. Invalid references should block the entire operation, including partial updates like updateIssue.

Removing a member suspends their status and archives their data.

Current members are active and unarchived. Invited users are excluded from current membership. Existing tests use active tenant users, so they remain valid. A cross-org label lookup needs an optional organization parameter.

I'll add unscoped finders for labels, issues, and comments. The label repository will get `findLabelById(labelId)` without organization filtering, paired with `assertOrgScope`. Issues and comments need similar internal helpers to avoid ugly naming like `findIssueByIdUnscoped`.

The label repository will expose `findLabelsByIds(labelIds)` without organization filtering, returning rows with their orgId. A cross-tenant query that omits org_id is a security leak; the service should classify the error and throw rather than return data. Parent issues in other organizations also require unscoped lookups.

Issue and comment repositories will expose unscoped lookups as `findIssueAnyOrg` and `findCommentAnyOrg`. Each service needs validation helpers. The `listLabelsForIssues` query must filter by `labels.orgId` to prevent foreign labels from appearing.

Label IDs live only in the join table, so filtering the join row during reads is sufficient. The stale label picker bug concerns writes attaching wrong labels; display filtering remains necessary to prevent foreign labels from appearing. When updateIssue receives no labelIds, it leaves existing labels untouched; when provided, it replaces the entire set after validating all IDs.

Parent issues are only set during creation. Assignees are handled by `createIssue` and `assignIssue`; updates do not modify them. Leads are set on create and update, but null or undefined values are skipped. Mention filtering will compare resolved IDs against current members, though the 100-member limit in `listMembers` could cause misses.

I'll verify each client-provided member ID individually with `findMember` rather than relying on the 100-member page limit. Body-resolved mention IDs are already checked against that same page, so they remain valid. Only current members should be included; inactive or non-members from the client should be ignored.

Mention ordering will keep body-resolved IDs first, then valid client-provided member IDs. Parent comment validation must run before rate limit consumption so invalid parents never consume quota or insert data. Composer suggestions for members who have left the workspace should be filtered out.

Mentions will require `status === "active"` to exclude suspended members. Parent issues in other organizations return `TenantScopeError`; missing issues return `NotFoundError`, and archived issues return `NotFoundError` rather than `AlreadyArchived`. Same-project live issues are valid parents.

Self-parenting is impossible during issue creation because the new issue does not yet exist. Replies to replies are invalid and return NotFound. Parent comments must belong to the same issue; cross-issue references return NotFound, while cross-organization references return TenantScopeError. Archived comments return NotFound. Label validation checks all IDs first: any cross-organization label triggers TenantScopeError, and any missing label triggers NotFound.

content.thinking: The isDomainError test claims to recognize exactly the domain error classes, but it only checks a few are true and Error is false.

toAppError also fails to map ActionNotFoundError, since that error type carries a code property.

I'll add a NotFoundError check to toAppError before the generic Error fallback. Otherwise NotFoundError subclasses would be misclassified as internal errors.

isDomainError will remain unchanged because NotFoundError subclasses are not domain errors. I'm now implementing repository lookups using Drizzle unscoped select patterns. A lightweight existence check for issues must include archived status and cross-org visibility.

Server-side enforcement is the real fix.

Confirmed the members list filters archived users. NotFoundError will map to code "not_found" in toAppError and isDomainError. The comment service must retain its existing assertCan, assertOrgScope, emit, archivePatch, and consumeRateLimit calls.

Issue and project services must retain assertCan, assertOrgScope, emit, wouldExceedLimit, and assertNotArchived. When a parent is archived, the service throws NotFound rather than conflict. A new helper will verify that assignees are active members.

A new helper validates that a parent issue exists and belongs to the current organization. Users who are members of other organizations are correctly treated as not found.

The actor is passed to assertOrgScope for the parent issue check. A TenantScopeError is thrown when the parent belongs to a different organization. Archived or project-mismatched parents also return NotFoundError. An assertLabels helper is being drafted.

The assertLabels helper validates that every label ID exists and belongs to the current organization. It throws NotFoundError for missing labels and TenantScopeError for cross-organization labels. Duplicate IDs are allowed. The listLabelsForIssues query will filter results with orgPredicate. A findIssueByIdOnly helper is being considered for lookups without an organization scope.

A `findCommentByIdAnyOrg` helper is being added to look up comments across organizations. The comment service will validate parent comments by checking existence, organization scope, and that the parent is not archived, belongs to the correct issue, and has no parent itself. Mention validation is next.

A `resolveMentionedUsers` helper is being drafted. It gathers active member IDs from the repository, resolves mentions from the comment body, and validates any extra user IDs provided by the client against active membership.

The `resolveMentionedUsers` helper is being refined. Client-provided user IDs are now validated against active membership in the current organization. If a client ID is not already in the current page of members, it is fetched and checked for active status before inclusion. This ensures only valid, current members are mentioned.

Mention resolution will filter members to active status before parsing the comment body. This prevents suspended or invited users from being incorrectly mentioned.

Project lead validation is being added for both insert and update operations. The lead ID must belong to an active member in the current organization.

On update, the lead ID is only validated when explicitly provided; a null value clears the lead and is allowed. The update schema will make leadId optional and nullable.

Issue creation will validate parent and assignee references before inserting into the database. This prevents wasted issue numbers when validation fails, since nextIssueNumber is computed from existing records rather than consumed as a sequence.

Label validation will run before the repository call in both updateIssue and assignIssue so a bad label never changes the title or assignee. The member repository must be imported into the issue and project services, and NotFoundError needs to be added to the support imports. Comment mentions are only notified on creation, not updates. updateIssue will throw before emitting any event when validation fails.
NotFoundError will be mapped in toAppError without adding it to isDomainError. This avoids altering the exact domain error classes if tests rely on instanceof checks.

I will implement all edits now.

Mentioned user IDs remain unchanged on comment updates. Sub-issues may nest under other sub-issues; only comments must be top-level. Archived parents return not found. I will implement a cross-organization issue lookup without loading labels.
